newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes flat with focus on Oriente.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes flat with focus on Oriente.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices were flat with steady benchmarket grade midday Wednesday, though refiners expected discounts to fall as they offered South American grades to one another, they said.

West Coast spot crude traders focused on Oriente crude, an Ecuadorian grade, which Texaco offered for late April delivery at $1.35 to $1.40 a barrel under Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, traders said. The shipment holds 360,000 barrels.
"We're not the lowest offer out there," a trader said, noting that Glencore trading house offered at $1.50 under ANS.
The April cargo precedes two full cargoes due in May.
Texaco's offer follows its purchase of 400,000 barrels of ANS on Friday, which displaced the South American cargo. The price, $1.32 off May WTI, is 0.27-cent widening from the last deal.
Outright prices stood at $18.18/18.38 a barrel, flat with Tuesday.
A leading seller of ANS priced shipments at $0.95 cents under WTI.
Line 63 and California heavy crude markets remained well- supplied, with no deals reported Monday or Tuesday.
